Attribute.value:
title: .NET Base64 Decode and Byte-Array File Write Named in a Process-Access Call Trace
id: d45cafee-0934-456d-9471-1cefbe03602a
status: experimental
description: >-
  Retained as a record of an intended hunt, with no demonstrated telemetry source (see
  the definition). Detects a process-access event whose call trace names both FromBase64String
  and WriteAllBytes, from a source image ending in .exe, a pattern for decoding
  an embedded Base64 payload and writing it to disk that legitimate installers
  unpacking bundled resources also use. Nothing here tests that the written file
  is executed. The CallTrace field carries resolved method names only in some EDR
  or enriched telemetry; stock Sysmon records module and offset frames, so the rule
  cannot match on a default Sysmon profile.
references:
  - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/fleetagentadvanced-exe-detections/
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: '2026-01-12'
modified: '2026-10-11'
tags:
  - attack.stealth
  - attack.t1027
  - detection.emerging-threats
logsource:
  category: process_access
  product: windows
  definition: 'No telemetry source is demonstrated for this rule. It would need a process-access event whose CallTrace carries resolved .NET method names for both a decode and a file write; stock Sysmon CallTrace holds module and offset frames, so it cannot match there, and no EDR or enriched profile providing such an event has been named or shown.'
detection:
  selection:
    CallTrace|contains|all:
      - 'FromBase64String'
      - 'WriteAllBytes'
    SourceImage|endswith: '.exe'
  filter_legitimate:
    SourceImage|startswith:
      - 'C:\Program Files\'
      - 'C:\Windows\'
  condition: selection and not filter_legitimate
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installers using Base64-encoded resources
level: low
Attribute.comment: .NET Base64 Decode and File Write in a Process-Access Call Trace (No Telemetry Source Demonstrated) | TIER: Hunting | robustness 2 | confidence INSUFFICIENT | ATT&CK T1027 | rule hash 7694819d | https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/fleetagentadvanced-exe-detections/

Attribute.value:
title: FleetAgentAdvanced Persistence with Microsoft .NET Masquerading
id: ccf14e14-5328-4d1b-98b9-27088663076e
status: experimental
description: >-
  Detects creation of a Registry Run-key value whose data references Microsoft,
  .NET, and Runtime branding together while the value data also contains an
  AppData path — a location legitimate Microsoft .NET Runtime components never
  use. The rule does not test that the path ends in an executable or that the
  file exists.
  Hunting-tier: the masquerade branding is attacker-chosen and renameable, and
  the AppData-location half of the check is common among legitimate consumer
  auto-start software on its own.
references:
  - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/fleetagentadvanced-exe-detections/
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: '2026-01-12'
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.privilege-escalation
  - attack.stealth
  - attack.t1547.001
  - attack.t1036.005
  - detection.emerging-threats
logsource:
  category: registry_set
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetObject|contains: '\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\'
    Details|contains|all:
      - 'Microsoft'
      - '.NET'
      - 'Runtime'
    Details|contains: '\AppData\'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Unsigned .NET development tools using Microsoft/.NET/Runtime naming in AppData (verify legitimacy)
level: medium
Attribute.comment: FleetAgentAdvanced Persistence with Microsoft .NET Masquerading | TIER: Hunting | robustness 1 | confidence LOW | ATT&CK T1547.001, T1036.005 | rule hash 359c8053 | https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/fleetagentadvanced-exe-detections/

Attribute.value:
title: FleetAgentAdvanced-Style .NET Runtime Optimization Scheduled Task Creation (Base Rule)
id: 2e8398f6-7a6a-4a8d-8aa2-f0cbbb346af5
name: fleetagentadvanced_schtasks_masquerade_create
status: experimental
description: >-
  Base rule (not alerting on its own): schtasks.exe invoked with /create and a
  command line referencing the ".NET Runtime Optimization" masquerade phrase.
  Paired with the task.xml-deletion base rule below via the correlation rule,
  which flags the create-then-delete anti-forensics sequence characteristic of
  this dropper family.
references:
  - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/fleetagentadvanced-exe-detections/
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: '2026-01-12'
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.privilege-escalation
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1053.005
  - detection.emerging-threats
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/create'
      - '.NET Runtime Optimization'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - >-
    Legitimate .NET Framework maintenance tasks using this exact phrase are not
    expected — verify digital signature if reviewed in isolation. Not alerting
    on its own; reviewed only in combination with the paired task.xml-deletion
    base rule.
level: informational
---
title: task.xml Deletion by Non-System Process (Base Rule)
id: 047f19e5-e1a1-484c-b825-24fb822125a5
name: fleetagentadvanced_taskxml_deletion
status: experimental
description: >-
  Base rule (not alerting on its own): deletion of a file named exactly
  task.xml by a process outside System32/SysWOW64. Paired with the
  scheduled-task-creation base rule above via the correlation rule below.
references:
  - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/fleetagentadvanced-exe-detections/
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: '2026-01-12'
tags:
  - attack.stealth
  - attack.t1070.004
  - detection.emerging-threats
logsource:
  category: file_delete
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\task.xml'
    Image|contains: '.exe'
  filter_legitimate:
    Image|contains:
      - '\System32\'
      - '\SysWOW64\'
  condition: selection and not filter_legitimate
falsepositives:
  - >-
    Legitimate installers or maintenance scripts that export and then delete a
    scheduled-task XML file named task.xml (uncommon). Not alerting on its
    own; reviewed only in combination with the paired scheduled-task-creation
    base rule.
level: informational
---
title: FleetAgentAdvanced-Class Scheduled Task Create-Then-Delete Anti-Forensics Sequence
id: 049f9083-fc9c-4c12-94d0-13538a2cc3cc
status: experimental
description: >-
  Fires when the ".NET Runtime Optimization" masquerade scheduled-task
  creation is followed by a task.xml deletion by a non-system process on the
  same host within a short window (creation first, then deletion). Neither base signal alone is reliable — the
  masquerade phrase is attacker-chosen and renameable, and a bare task.xml
  deletion has no inherent malicious meaning — but this dropper family creates
  the scheduled task and deletes its exported task.xml within roughly 120
  milliseconds as a deliberate anti-forensics step, a sequence a coincidental
  unrelated program is not expected to reproduce.
references:
  - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/fleetagentadvanced-exe-detections/
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: '2026-01-12'
modified: '2026-10-11'
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.privilege-escalation
  - attack.execution
  - attack.stealth
  - attack.t1053.005
  - attack.t1070.004
  - detection.emerging-threats
correlation:
  type: temporal_ordered
  rules:
    - fleetagentadvanced_schtasks_masquerade_create
    - fleetagentadvanced_taskxml_deletion
  group-by:
    - host.name
  timespan: 5m
falsepositives:
  - >-
    A future build renaming both the masquerade phrase and the exported XML
    filename evades this correlation entirely — both remain the same
    attacker-chosen naming decision, so this is a scoping lead for this
    specific build family, not a durable technique-level detector.
level: medium
Attribute.comment: FleetAgentAdvanced Scheduled-Task Masquerade Creation and task.xml Deletion (Correlation) | TIER: Hunting | robustness 2 | confidence LOW — both base signals are individually brittle, masquerade-literal-dependent selectors; the correlation adds real but limited value | ATT&CK T1053.005, T1070.004 | rule hash 38a49f0d | https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/fleetagentadvanced-exe-detections/

Attribute.value:
title: Remote Thread Created by a FleetAgentAdvanced Binary or an AppData Process
id: 1ca5cfa6-f7af-4dde-80b1-87edbf3c637b
status: experimental
description: >-
    Detects a remote thread created in another process (Sysmon create-remote-thread
    event) by a process image named RuntimeOptimization.exe or FleetAgentAdvanced.exe,
    or by any process image running from AppData and not from Program Files. The
    FleetAgentAdvanced report records the remote-injection APIs as present in the
    binary and never seen firing, so this is a lead for that capability and not a
    detection of an observed injection. It replaces an earlier selector that looked
    for the API names VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory and CreateRemoteThread in
    the process-access CallTrace field; Sysmon records module and offset frames
    there and not function names, so that selector could not match stock Sysmon.
references:
    - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/fleetagentadvanced-exe-detections/
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: '2026-01-12'
modified: '2026-10-11'
tags:
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.stealth
    - attack.t1055
    - detection.emerging-threats
logsource:
    category: create_remote_thread
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_family:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\RuntimeOptimization.exe'
            - '\FleetAgentAdvanced.exe'
    selection_appdata:
        SourceImage|contains: '\AppData\'
    filter_legitimate:
        SourceImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: 1 of selection_* and not filter_legitimate
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate development tools and debuggers from AppData
level: medium
Attribute.comment: Remote Thread Created by a FleetAgentAdvanced Binary or an AppData Process | TIER: Hunting | robustness 2 | confidence LOW | ATT&CK T1055 | rule hash 24e908ec | https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/fleetagentadvanced-exe-detections/

import "hash"

rule MAL_FleetAgentAdvanced_Dropper_Hash_Function_Combo {
   meta:
      description = "Detects FleetAgentAdvanced.exe dropper via exact file hash, or via a combination of at least 3 of 6 distinctive, operator-coined internal .NET method names (DropEmbeddedAgent, SetPersistence, CreateShortcut, StartWatchdog, RunWatchdog, InjectIntoProcess) that survive a masquerade-branding rebrand."
      license = "CC BY 4.0 - https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/"
      author = "The Hunters Ledger"
      reference = "https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/fleetagentadvanced-exe-detections/"
      date = "2026-01-12"
      hash1 = "172258e53b9506a7671deab25d2ad360cd833a4942609f1a4836d305ffe4578b"
      family = "FleetAgentAdvanced"
      malware_type = "Dropper-Trojan"
      campaign = "Arsenal-237-109.230.231.37-Malware-Repository"
      id = "bf7dbbc0-99af-557d-96a8-69a6247efa88"
   strings:
      $func1 = "DropEmbeddedAgent" ascii wide
      $func2 = "SetPersistence" ascii wide
      $func3 = "CreateShortcut" ascii wide
      $func4 = "StartWatchdog" ascii wide
      $func5 = "RunWatchdog" ascii wide
      $func6 = "InjectIntoProcess" ascii wide
   condition:
      uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and
      filesize < 500KB and
      (
         hash.sha256(0, filesize) == "172258e53b9506a7671deab25d2ad360cd833a4942609f1a4836d305ffe4578b" or
         3 of ($func*)
      )
}
Attribute.comment: FleetAgentAdvanced Dropper Hash and Coined Function-Name Combination | TIER: Detection | robustness 2 | confidence HIGH | ATT&CK T1027, T1547.001, T1053.005, T1055 | rule hash 43d9bfe3 | https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/fleetagentadvanced-exe-detections/

Attribute.value:
rule SUSP_FleetAgentAdvanced_NET_Masquerade_Combination {
   meta:
      description = "Detects PE files (the rule does not test for a .NET or CLR header) combining FleetAgentAdvanced-style configuration variable names (WATCHDOG_MUTEX, AGENT_SECRET, EMBEDDED_AGENT, etc.) or generic process-injection API references with the Microsoft .NET Runtime Optimization masquerade strings. Brittle to a masquerade-naming rebrand — treat as a scoping lead, not an alert."
      license = "CC BY 4.0 - https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/"
      author = "The Hunters Ledger"
      reference = "https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/fleetagentadvanced-exe-detections/"
      date = "2026-01-12"
      modified = "2026-10-11"
      family = "FleetAgentAdvanced"
      malware_type = "Dropper-Trojan-Masquerade-Component"
      campaign = "Arsenal-237-109.230.231.37-Malware-Repository"
      id = "4a8d104a-d581-5c8b-bd16-1c72215b0e87"
   strings:
      $config1 = "EMBEDDED_AGENT" ascii wide
      $config2 = "INSTALL_NAME" ascii wide
      $config3 = "STARTUP_NAME" ascii wide
      $config4 = "WATCHDOG_MUTEX" ascii wide
      $config5 = "MUTEX_NAME" ascii wide
      $config6 = "SERVER_HOST" ascii wide
      $config7 = "AGENT_SECRET" ascii wide

      $persist1 = "RuntimeOptimization.exe" ascii wide
      $persist2 = "Microsoft .NET Runtime Optimization" ascii wide
      $persist3 = "Microsoft\\CLR" ascii wide

      $api1 = "VirtualAllocEx" ascii
      $api2 = "WriteProcessMemory" ascii
      $api3 = "CreateRemoteThread" ascii
      $api4 = "NtUnmapViewOfSection" ascii
      $api5 = "PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE" ascii
   condition:
      uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and
      filesize < 500KB and
      (
         (2 of ($config*) and any of ($persist*)) or
         (any of ($api*) and any of ($persist*))
      )
}
Attribute.comment: FleetAgentAdvanced .NET Masquerade Configuration and API Combination | TIER: Hunting | robustness 1 | confidence LOW | ATT&CK T1036.005, T1055 | rule hash ec973ae9 | https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/fleetagentadvanced-exe-detections/
